title: Forgetting a Name
short: Admit it lightly ("I'm so sorry, your name has slipped my mind"), or introduce yourself first so they offer theirs; help others when they forget yours.
trouble: Learners avoid the person or skip an introduction to hide the lapse. A brief, cheerful admission is better than an awkward evasion.

blocks.html: Everyone forgets a name sometimes, often right after an introduction. What matters is how gracefully you handle it, and how kindly you help others when they forget yours.
Admit it lightly ("I'm so sorry, your name has slipped my mind"), or introduce yourself first so the other person offers theirs. When someone forgets your name, say it for them.

A forgotten name is a tiny slip that everyone understands. Trying to hide it, by avoiding the person or skipping an introduction, makes the moment far more awkward and can leave someone out. A light admission takes two seconds, and offering your own name first gives the other person an easy chance to say theirs. Helping someone who has forgotten your name spares them the same discomfort.

say: Hi! I'm Sam. We met at Priya's party last spring.
Of course! I'm Nora. It's so good to see you again.
opts.narr: Sam offers his name first, and Nora offers hers.

blocks.title: A name you can't recall
blocks.q: At a reunion, Ruby greets a classmate whose name she has completely forgotten. Her friend Leo walks up. What can she do?
steps: She can say to the classmate, "This is my friend Leo," and pause; the classmate will usually say their name.
Or she admits it lightly: "I'm so sorry, your name has slipped my mind."
She does not skip the introduction and leave Leo standing.
blocks.a: Introduce Leo and pause, or admit it lightly.

blocks.title: When they forget yours
blocks.q: Mr. Diaz greets Omar warmly but clearly can't remember his name. What should Omar do?
steps: Help him: "Hi, Mr. Diaz, it's Omar Haddad. You coached my soccer team."
The detail jogs his memory and spares him the awkward search.
blocks.a: Say his own name and a detail.

blocks.name: et-intro
blocks.cap: Once the name comes back, finish the introduction: step through it.

blocks.html: Avoiding the person or skipping an introduction to hide the lapse. A brief, cheerful admission is better than an awkward evasion. Quick check: is someone standing unintroduced because you forgot a name? Fix it now.
